title: btatt: Make the handle-UUID mapping device-aware
description:
Currently, the mapping is only "direction-aware". Which means
the dissector basically assumes there's only ever one remote ATT server
connected to the local Host. Which means that handles can get mis-translated
when multiple remote servers are connected.

This change ensures that the mappings are instead stored on per-device basis,
using that device/server's BD_ADDR as a key.

-------

To demonstrate the difference:

* Connect the local Central to a remote Peripheral A
* Carry out GATT service discovery on A and then read some arbitrary handles (ideally after GAP + GATT) on that server.
* Connect the local Central to another remote Peripheral B. This should best be a different product from A, to ensure they have different handle mappings.
* Carry out GATT service discovery on B.
* Read the same handles on A again.

(In the trace below, Peripheral A = `HP_da...`, Peripheral B = `Dongguan...`)

Before the proposed changes, you'll notice that after B got connected (around frame 293), some of A's handles are translated incorrectly into B's UUIDs. In this case, handle 0xd should've been a Characteristic User Description belonging to some HP service:

![image](/uploads/680d81e88ba80ed75f783cca6b78e173/image.png){width=900 height=376}

Whereas after the proposed changes, A's handles are now translated correctly every time -- regardless of B getting connected:

![image](/uploads/41ec1b43ac3e77fe075b1bb460c50788/image.png){width=900 height=322}

The sample snoop is attached: [btsnoop_truncated2.log](/uploads/91c5c5cdeeb4329c80ae7c98850c55a9/btsnoop_truncated2.log)
